root_cause: Console._write_buffer copies self._buffer into self._record_buffer every time it runs, including while _buffer_index > 0 (inside console.capture() or a `with console:` block). _exit_buffer -> _check_buffer -> _write_buffer runs after every print, but the buffer is only cleared when _buffer_index == 0 or in end_capture. So each print inside a capture appends the whole accumulated buffer to the record again (Print 1 / Print 1, Print 2 / ...). Captured output, which never reaches the terminal, also ends up recorded.
best_solution: Gate the record side effect on the same condition that actually flushes output: in _write_buffer change `if self.record:` to `if self.record and not self._buffer_index:`. At buffer index 0 the buffer holds exactly what is about to be written to the file, and it is recorded once. end_capture renders and clears the buffer before _exit_buffer drops the index to 0, so captured text is never recorded. The recording then mirrors terminal output, and nested `with console:` blocks are recorded once instead of repeatedly.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that stops appending to _record_buffer while _buffer_index > 0, for example moving the extend into the `if self._buffer_index == 0:` branch. Deduplicating alone (recording only new segments, or recording the captured text once in end_capture) fails, because the test requires captured output to be left out of the recording entirely.

our_outcome_summary:
All of v4/v6/v7/v8 failed in the Kaggle env. v4 and v6 committed only repro scripts (reproduce_issue.py, repro_fix.py) and no source change. Both repros put a single print inside capture, which cannot show the accumulation. v6 also asserted recorded == captured, the wrong semantics, copied from the old existing test. v7 produced an empty patch. v8 changed the export_text/export_html asserts to `self.record or self._record_buffer`, which is the wrong location and does nothing for the bug. The hidden test failed with a record of 'Print 0
Print 1
Print 1
Print 2
Print 1
Print 2
Print 3
...'.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a title and an issue link you cannot open, build a repro that repeats the operation 3 or more times inside the context manager, because accumulation and duplication bugs never show on a single call. Then trace the write path for a side effect (copy to a record, log or cache sink) that runs on every call while the primary buffer is cleared only under a condition, and gate the side effect on that same flush condition. Existing tests in the area may encode the old semantics the fix is meant to change. For interaction bugs between two features, prefer the semantics where the secondary sink mirrors what actually reaches the real output. Never ship a repro script as the only diff.
